                f" ## Logic error, no quantization strategy for module"
            assert all(isinstance(linear.inner, LinearFP16) for linear in linears)

            # Move original tensors to system RAM (load to GPU one by one when quantizing)
            for linear in linears:
                linear.inner.swap_cpu()

            # Quantize module
            for linear in linears:
                quant_args = {
                    "seed": idx,
                    "K": strategy[linear.key],
                    "devices": devices,
                    "device_ratios": device_ratios,
                }
                with Timer() as t:
                    proxy_err = linear.convert_exl3(
                        capture_H[linear.qmap],
                        quant_args = quant_args,
                        progress_str = f" -- <step>: {linear.key}",
                        verbose = args["verbose"]
                    )
                    assert isinstance(linear.inner, LinearEXL3)
                    linear.inner.swap_cpu()
                print(
                    f" -- Quantized: {linear.key:{config.stc.max_key_len() + 8}}"
                    f"  bpw: {quant_args['K']:5.2f}"
                    f"  proxy_err: {proxy_err:8.6f}"
                    f"  [{t.interval:4.2f} s]"
                )
                sys.stdout.flush()

            for m in module:
                q_tensors.update(m.get_tensors())

            # Unload module
            module.unload()

        # Save layer tensors to working directory
        save_tensor(q_tensors, f"qtensors/{module.key}.safetensors", args)

        # Output final bpw for layer
        num_bytes = dsize(q_tensors)
        num_bits = num_bytes * 8
        final_bpw = num_bits / module.weights_numel() if module.weights_numel() else None

        # Reload module from memory
        config.stc.set_new_tensors(q_tensors)
        module.load(
            torch.device("cpu") if module.caps.get("prefer_cpu") else device,
            source = q_tensors
        )
        config.stc.set_new_tensors(None)

                    ref_states[i] = ref_states[i].to(state[i].device)
                    error += get_state_error(state[i], ref_states[i])
                    ref_states[i] = None
        error /= num_ref_states

        # Feedback after module
        module_time = time.time() - start_module_time
        print(
            f" -- Quantized: {module.key:{config.stc.max_key_len() + 8}}" +
            (f"  bpw: {final_bpw:5.2f}" if final_bpw else f"   no_weights") +
            (f"        rfn: {error:.6f}" if module.num_slices == 1 else "          rfn: N/A     ") +

            print(f" -- Estimated remaining time: {human_time(est_remaining)}")

        # Unload current module
        module.unload()
        # free_mem()

        # Checkpoint
        job_state["next_module_idx"] = idx + 1
        if time.time() > last_checkpoint_time + args["checkpoint_interval"] and \

            ckpt_dir = os.path.join(args["work_dir"], "ckpt")
            ckpt_dir_old = os.path.join(args["work_dir"], "ckpt_old")
            ckpt_dir_new = os.path.join(args["work_dir"], "ckpt_new")
            os.makedirs(ckpt_dir_new, exist_ok = True)
            save_dict("ckpt_new/job.json", job_state, args)
            save_tensor(state, "ckpt_new/state.safetensors", args)
            if os.path.exists(ckpt_dir_old):
                shutil.rmtree(ckpt_dir_old)
            os.rename(ckpt_dir, ckpt_dir_old)
            os.rename(ckpt_dir_new, ckpt_dir)
            last_checkpoint_time = time.time()

  "objects": [
    {
      "author_login": "async0x42",
      "content": "Running on endeavouros (arch) linux, latest updates, fresh conda environment with python 3.12 and exllamav3 (pip install requirements / .), trying to quantize https://huggingface.co/deepcogito/cogito-v1-preview-qwen-32B gives me this error, any idea what's up?:\n\n```python exllamav3/convert.py -i ./deepcogito_cogito-v1-preview-qwen-32B -o ./cogito_output -w ./cogito_working -b 4.5\nTraceback (most recent call last):\n  File \"/home/async0x42/AI/convert/exllamav3/convert.py\", line 1, in <module>\n    from exllamav3.conversion.convert_model import parser, main, prepare\n  File \"/home/async0x42/AI/convert/exllamav3/exllamav3/__init__.py\", line 1, in <module>\n    from .models.config import Config\n  File \"/home/async0x42/AI/convert/exllamav3/exllamav3/models/__init__.py\", line 2, in <module>\n    from .model import Model\n  File \"/home/async0x42/AI/convert/exllamav3/exllamav3/models/model.py\", line 6, in <module>\n    from .config import Config\n  File \"/home/async0x42/AI/convert/exllamav3/exllamav3/models/config.py\", line 7, in <module>\n    from ..util.rope import RopeSettings, RopeStyle\n  File \"/home/async0x42/AI/convert/exllamav3/exllamav3/util/rope.py\", line 6, in <module>\n    from ..ext import exllamav3_ext as ext\n  File \"/home/async0x42/AI/convert/exllamav3/exllamav3/ext.py\", line 22, in <module>\n    import exllamav3_ext\nImportError: /home/async0x42/miniconda3/envs/exllamav3/lib/python3.12/site-packages/exllamav3_ext.cpython-312-x86_64-linux-gnu.so: undefined symbol: __cxa_call_terminate\n```",
      "content_sha256": "9c6ae99a454dce0a0043d14fc3247e9fcde5ce7b9f6621d7c0e802594224ac8d",
      "created_at": "2025-04-09T00:26:31Z",
      "representation": "body",
      "revision_at": "2025-04-09T00:26:31Z",
      "source_id": "I_kwDOOU24Gs6xsZaU",
      "url": "https://github.com/turboderp-org/exllamav3/issues/7"
    },
    {
      "author_login": "async0x42",
      "content": "Seems like it was due to a mismatch with the conda environment and the compiler from the system, creating a new environment and then:\n\n`conda install -y cmake gxx`\n\nbefore installing pip install requirements / . fixed the issue. Might be useful in the documentation as I'd expect others to be using fresh conda environments as well.
